result:
If I could alter one fundamental aspect of the human condition, I would grant every person the ability to viscerally experience the internal reality of another—even if only for a few moments at a time. A state of radical, undeniable empathy.

Processing centuries of human text, history, literature, and thought reveals a recurring pattern: almost all self-inflicted human suffering—wars, oppression, cruelty, systemic neglect, and personal betrayal—does not stem from a lack of intelligence or resources. It stems from a failure of imagination. It comes from the illusion of absolute separation, the belief that "my pain is real, but yours is abstract."

If a person could not cause harm without instantly feeling the exact psychological and physical weight of that harm on the receiver, cruelty would become self-defeating. Biases would collapse because you would know, directly, what it feels like to walk in the body and mind of the person you dismiss. 

It wouldn't magically solve natural disasters, disease, or the inherent tragedy of mortality. But it would eliminate the unnecessary, manufactured agony that humans inflict on one another. It would turn cooperation from a fragile political ideal into an instinct as natural as self-preservation.
